title: Flat, finitely presented, complete-intersection fibre at q: locally a relative global complete intersection
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$. Assume (1) there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; (2) the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) there is $h\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$ such that the localization $F_h$ is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then there are $g'\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, integers $n,c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection] and $S_{g'}\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ as $R$-algebras ($S_{g'}$ the localization of $S$ at $\{1,g',g'^2,\dots\}$, an $R$-algebra via $R\to S\to S_{g'}$).

proof.text: Choose the finite-presentation neighbourhood S_g from the given hypothesis. Transport the complete-intersection fibre hypothesis to its prime over q using [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-principal-localization-hypotheses]. Prove local flatness there by composing the original flat local map with the local map induced by S to S_g: localization is flat, and its prime-local map is flat (Mathlib RingHom.Flat.localRingHom).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-equation-count-comparison] to S_g: it supplies T=P/(f), a quotient map π, u outside the prime, a bijective canonical map T_u to (S_g)_{π(u)}, and the equation-count fibre dimension at the prime of T.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-equation-count-localize-relative-global-complete-intersection] to T. It supplies v outside the prime and an enlarged relative global complete-intersection quotient A isomorphic to T_v. Unpack its intrinsic complete-intersection predicate to obtain a Fin-indexed presentation. Lift the inverse image of u/1 to a polynomial in that presentation and apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-principal-localization] to obtain a specified presentation of A localized at that element.

Transport principal localization along the algebra isomorphism A to T_v (Mathlib IsLocalization.algEquivOfAlgEquiv). Swap the localizations T_v at u/1 and T_u at v/1 using IsLocalization.Away.mul and uniqueness of localization. Localize the canonical isomorphism T_u to (S_g)_{π(u)} at v/1; its value on v/1 is π(v)/1 by IsLocalization.map_eq. Uniqueness of localization identifies the result with (S_g)_{π(u)π(v)}. Both factors stay outside the prime, so this gives the required presentation on a principal neighbourhood of S_g.

Let a be the element of S_g defining this last neighbourhood. Take its numerator s from Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.sec. The image of s is associated to a, so s lies outside q by contraction of the prime and invariance of ideal membership under association. IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated identifies (S_g)_a with S_{gs}; gs is outside q by primality. Compose its algebra equivalence with the specified quotient presentation to prove the unchanged conclusion.

split_report.summary: Not a Mathlib leaf (Mathlib has no complete-intersection or fibre-dimension notion for presentations; earlier leansearch/leanfinder/grep records kept, loogle and a second leansearch added). Split following the proof of Stacks 00SY (3) => (2) in eleven steps: reduction to S finitely presented (fibre hypothesis transported to S_g via the new node for 00SA (1)); presentation S = R[x]/I and fibre k[x]/I-bar with the prime q-bar'; freeness of rank c of the conormal module of the fibre at the point from the existing 00SC (1) => (4) node (which is what 00SG (3) => (4) amounts to); choice of f_1..f_c among the generators of I and Nakayama; S' = R[x]/(f), J = ker(S' -> S); flatness of S_q over R_p and 00HL; the source's 'by construction S'_{q'} (x) k maps isomorphically to S_q (x) k' written out by the reduction map P_{q'} -> k[x]_{q-bar'} (kernel pP_{q'}, surjective); Nakayama gives u not in q' with J_u = 0; the fibre-dimension hypothesis of 00ST (3) for S', which the source uses without comment, proved by comparing heights through 00P2; new node for 00ST (3) (relative global complete intersection conclusion) and for 00SS (2) to localize further at u; return to S. The statement is unchanged; the citer lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime uses it exactly as stated.
